title: The Dhamaal Boys Are Back, Louder and Dumber Than Ever. Dhamaal 4 Lands July 10 and Refuses to Apologise.
excerpt: Ajay Devgn, Riteish Deshmukh, Arshad Warsi and Jaaved Jaaferi reunite for Indra Kumar's fourth treasure hunt — and the new Guru Randhawa banger 'Qeher' is exactly as unserious as you'd hope.
body:
Some franchises grow up. Some franchises win Oscars. And then there is **Dhamaal**, which has spent nearly two decades doing exactly one thing — throwing a pack of grown men at a pile of money and watching them fall over each other — and has the audacity to keep getting away with it. The fourth instalment, cheerfully subtitled **Qeher**, arrives in cinemas worldwide on **July 10, 2026**, and based on everything the makers have dropped this week, it is not here to reinvent the wheel. It's here to roll the wheel down a hill and laugh.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y</youtube>

This week's offering is the song **'Qeher'**, sung by **Guru Randhawa**, and it is precisely the kind of glorious, brain-off chaos the title promises. The **Dhamaal** boys — **Ajay Devgn**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Riteish Deshmukh** and **Jaaved Jaaferi** — show up in their quirky best, soaking in full Guru fever, executing an infectious hook step choreographed by Piyush and Shazia like men who know the dance reels write themselves. **Ketika Sharma** glides in for a special appearance. It's bright, it's loud, it's stitched together by producer-arranger Sanjoy into a track engineered for one purpose: getting stuck in your head before the film even opens. It follows last week's equally unhinged 'Chatni,' and together they make the marketing strategy crystal clear — flood the timeline with earworms, let the franchise nostalgia do the rest.


And the nostalgia is real. **Indra Kumar** returns to direct, **Ajay Devgn** produces alongside Bhushan and Krishan Kumar under the T-Series-Devgn Films banner, and the ensemble has swelled into a genuine powerhouse: **Sanjay Mishra**, **Ravi Kishan**, **Upendra Limaye**, **Esha Gupta**, **Sanjeeda Shaikh** and **Anjali Anand** all join the treasure hunt. Anand, in a recent chat, said she was "born dancing" for songs like 'Chatni' and called it the "ultimate chatpata song." That's the energy of this entire production — everyone in on the joke, nobody pretending it's anything other than a family entertainer built to make a packed Friday-night hall roar.

Let's be honest about the franchise's track record, because it's a funny one. The first **Dhamaal** (2007) wasn't a theatrical smash but grew into a TV-rerun institution. **Double Dhamaal** opened well in 2011 and then fizzled. It wasn't until **Total Dhamaal** in 2019 that the series landed its first genuine box-office hit. So **Dhamaal 4** arrives carrying both goodwill and a question mark. Trade trackers at Pinkvilla are forecasting a first-day haul of roughly Rs. 14-19 crore — a healthy opening that leans entirely on franchise value and the broad-comedy hunger that's been underserved this year. The trailer, out a few days ago, did its job: enough gags landed to convince the family audience this is a worthwhile outing.

Here's my take. In a season crowded with partition epics, spy universes and prestige OTT dramas, there is something almost refreshing about a film that wants nothing from you except two and a half hours of switching your brain off. **Dhamaal** has never been cool. It has never tried to be. And for a certain kind of diaspora household — the one where three generations crowd onto one sofa and the only requirement is that nobody has to read subtitles or think too hard — that's not a weakness. It's the entire pitch.

**Where to watch, diaspora edition:** Dhamaal 4 releases in cinemas worldwide on July 10, 2026 (some trade listings cite July 17 — watch your local chain for the confirmed date). Expect wide US, UK, Canada and Gulf bookings through the major desi-cinema distributors, because broad Hindi comedy is reliable overseas business and a mid-July weekend is prime family-outing territory. No OTT partner has been announced yet, but the franchise has historically landed on streaming within a few months of release — so if you miss the theatre run, a couch viewing won't be far behind.

Is it going to be good? That is, gloriously, beside the point. Is it going to be fun? The hook step already answered that.
